# 12-Week Resistance Training Programme for PCOS Management
**Client: 31F | PCOS (Rotterdam criteria) | HbA1c 5.8 | BMI 28 | Start: 1 June 2026**

---

## PROGRAMME OVERVIEW

This 12-week programme prioritises **metabolic health and insulin sensitivity** through structured resistance training, with careful attention to energy balance and recovery—critical for PCOS management. The endocrinologist's recommendation for resistance training as first-line therapy is supported by evidence showing that strength training improves insulin sensitivity independent of weight loss.

**Key Principles:**
- Progressive overload without excessive volume (under-fuelling risk is real)
- Emphasis on compound movements and lower-body work (largest muscle groups)
- Adequate recovery and nutrition to support hormonal health
- Monitoring of cycle regularity and subjective wellbeing as success markers
- Flexibility to adjust based on energy levels and menstrual patterns

---

## PHASE STRUCTURE

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Training Split |
|-------|-------|-------|-----------------|
| **Phase 1: Foundation** | 1–4 | Movement quality, work capacity, baseline strength | 3 days/week, full-body |
| **Phase 2: Hypertrophy & Metabolic Stress** | 5–8 | Muscle building, insulin sensitivity, moderate volume | 4 days/week, upper/lower split |
| **Phase 3: Strength & Consolidation** | 9–12 | Strength gains, metabolic resilience, deload integration | 4 days/week, upper/lower split |

---

## PHASE 1: FOUNDATION (WEEKS 1–4)

**Objective:** Establish movement patterns, build work capacity, assess baseline strength and recovery tolerance.

**Training Structure:** 3 sessions per week, full-body, Monday/Wednesday/Friday (or equivalent with 48-hour recovery).

**Session Duration:** 45–50 minutes (including warm-up).

**Rationale:** Three days allows adequate recovery between sessions while building consistency. Full-body sessions maximise metabolic stimulus with lower total volume, reducing under-fuelling risk. Compound movements activate large muscle groups (glutes, quads, back, chest) which are insulin-sensitive tissues.

---

### WEEK 1

**Session A (Monday) – Lower Emphasis**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Tempo | Rest | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|------|-------|
| Goblet Squat | 3 | 8–10 | 3-1-2 | 90s | Light weight; focus on depth and control |
| Romanian Deadlift (RDL) | 3 | 8–10 | 3-1-2 | 90s | Moderate weight; feel hamstring/glute stretch |
| Chest Press (DB or machine) | 3 | 10–12 | 2-1-2 | 75s | Controlled, no lockout bounce |
| Inverted Row or Lat Pulldown | 3 | 10–12 | 2-1-2 | 75s | Scapular retraction focus |
| Pallof Press (or anti-rotation hold) | 2 | 10 each side | 2-1-2 | 60s | Core stability, light resistance |

**Session B (Wednesday) – Upper Emphasis**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Tempo | Rest | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|------|-------|
| Leg Press or Belt Squat | 3 | 10–12 | 2-1-2 | 90s | Easier on lower back; good for volume |
| Leg Curl (machine or lying) | 3 | 10–12 | 2-1-2 | 75s | Hamstring isolation; controlled eccentric |
| Incline DB Press | 3 | 8–10 | 2-1-2 | 90s | Upper chest and anterior shoulder |
| Seal Row or Machine Row | 3 | 10–12 | 2-1-2 | 75s | Chest-supported; reduces lower back demand |
| Face Pulls | 2 | 12–15 | 2-1-2 | 60s | Shoulder health, rear delt |

**Session C (Friday) – Balanced Full-Body**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Tempo | Rest | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|------|-------|
| Trap Bar Deadlift (or conventional) | 3 | 6–8 | 3-1-2 | 2min | Heaviest lift; full recovery |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 | 8 each leg | 2-1-2 | 90s | Unilateral; glute and quad emphasis |
| Push-up (incline or flat) | 3 | 8–12 | 2-1-2 | 75s | Chest, shoulders, triceps |
| Bent-Over Barbell Row | 3 | 8–10 | 2-1-2 | 90s | Back thickness; posterior chain |
| Sled Push or Leg Press (light) | 2 | 12–15 | 2-0-2 | 60s | Metabolic finisher; light weight |

**Week 1 Notes:**
- Use RPE 6–7/10 (moderate effort, 2–3 reps in reserve).
- Prioritise form over load; video yourself or use mirrors.
- Track all weights and reps in a log.
- No cardio this week; focus on resistance training adaptation.

---

### WEEK 2

**Repeat Week 1 structure, increasing weights by 2.5–5 lbs (1–2 kg) on compound lifts if form was solid.**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Adjustment |
|----------|------|------|------------|
| Goblet Squat | 3 | 8–10 | +2.5 lbs |
| RDL | 3 | 8–10 | +5 lbs |
| Chest Press | 3 | 10–12 | +2.5 lbs |
| Inverted Row | 3 | 10–12 | +2.5 lbs |
| Leg Press | 3 | 10–12 | +5 lbs |
| Incline DB Press | 3 | 8–10 | +2.5 lbs |
| Trap Bar Deadlift | 3 | 6–8 | +5–10 lbs |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 | 8 each | +2.5 lbs |

**Week 2 Notes:**
- Assess energy levels and recovery. If fatigued, maintain weights rather than increase.
- Begin tracking menstrual cycle phase (if applicable) and subjective energy/mood.
- Introduce light walking (20–30 min, 2–3 times) on non-training days if energy permits.

---

### WEEK 3

**Repeat Week 2 weights, aiming for 1–2 additional reps per set if possible.**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Target |

| Goblet Squat | 3 | 9–11 | +1 rep |
| RDL | 3 | 9–11 | +1 rep |
| Chest Press | 3 | 11–13 | +1 rep |
| Inverted Row | 3 | 11–13 | +1 rep |
| Leg Press | 3 | 11–13 | +1 rep |
| Incline DB Press | 3 | 9–11 | +1 rep |
| Trap Bar Deadlift | 3 | 7–9 | +1 rep |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 | 9 each | +1 rep |

**Week 3 Notes:**
- Check in on energy, hunger, and cycle regularity.
- If cycle is still irregular but energy is good, maintain current nutrition.
- If fatigued or hungry, increase calorie intake (see Nutrition section below).

---

### WEEK 4 – DELOAD

**Objective:** Reduce fatigue, consolidate adaptations, assess readiness for Phase 2.

**Structure:** Same 3 sessions, but reduce volume and intensity.

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Tempo | Rest | Notes |

| RDL | 2 | 8 | 3-1-2 | 75s | Lighter weight, focus on form |

| Inverted Row | 2 | 10 | 2-1-2 | 60s | Reduced sets |

| Bulgarian Split Squat | 2 | 8 each | 2-1-2 | 75s | Reduced volume |

**Week 4 Notes:**
- Use RPE 5–6/10 (easy, 4+ reps in reserve).
- Prioritise sleep and nutrition.
- Assess subjective wellbeing, energy, and any changes in cycle regularity.
- Plan Phase 2 progression based on recovery and readiness.

---

## PHASE 2: HYPERTROPHY & METABOLIC STRESS (WEEKS 5–8)

**Objective:** Build muscle mass (insulin-sensitive tissue), improve metabolic health, increase training stimulus while maintaining energy balance.

**Training Structure:** 4 sessions per week, upper/lower split (Monday/Tuesday/Thursday/Friday, or equivalent).

**Rationale:** Four days allows higher volume while maintaining recovery. Upper/lower split distributes fatigue and allows more frequent stimulus to large muscle groups. Hypertrophy rep ranges (8–12 reps) and moderate rest periods create metabolic stress, which improves insulin sensitivity.

**Session Duration:** 50–60 minutes.

---

**Alcohol:**
- Limit to 0–1 drink per day (if any). Alcohol impairs glucose control and increases inflammation.

## CRITICAL PREAMBLE: CARDIO & PCOS

**⚠️ Important Consideration:**

Your client has expressed desire to "lose weight faster," which is understandable. However, **excessive cardio combined with under-fuelling is particularly problematic for PCOS clients** and can:

- **Worsen insulin resistance** (paradoxically, excessive exercise stress increases cortisol, which impairs insulin sensitivity).
- **Suppress reproductive hormones** (low energy availability suppresses LH/FSH, worsening cycle irregularity).
- **Increase inflammation** (overtraining increases systemic inflammation, worsening PCOS symptoms).
- **Reduce muscle mass** (cardio without adequate protein/calories causes muscle loss, reducing insulin-sensitive tissue).
- **Trigger metabolic adaptation** (aggressive calorie deficit + high cardio slows metabolism, making future weight loss harder).

**Evidence-Based Approach:**

Research on PCOS and weight loss shows:
- **Resistance training + modest calorie deficit (300–500 kcal/day) + adequate nutrition = optimal outcomes** for fat loss, cycle regularity, and metabolic health.
- **Excessive cardio (>5 hours/week) without adequate fuelling = worse outcomes** for PCOS symptoms and hormonal health.
- **Slow, steady fat loss (0.5–1 lb/week) = sustainable and preserves muscle + hormonal health.**

**Recommendation to Client:**

Frame weight loss as a **secondary benefit** of building metabolic health through resistance training and stable nutrition. The primary goal is:
1. Improve insulin sensitivity (HbA1c <5.7).
2. Restore cycle regularity.
3. Build muscle (insulin-sensitive tissue).
4. Improve energy and wellbeing.

**Fat loss will follow naturally** from these adaptations, typically 0.5–1 lb/week, which is sustainable and preserves hormonal health.

**Rationale:**
- LISS improves aerobic capacity and fat oxidation without excessive cortisol elevation.

## PHASE 2: HYPERTROPHY & METABOLIC STRESS (WEEKS 5–8) – MODERATE CARDIO

**Objective:** Support muscle building with resistance training; add moderate cardio for fat loss without compromising recovery.

**Cardio Prescription:**
- **Frequency:** 2–3 sessions/week.
- **Type:** LISS (low-intensity steady-state) + optional moderate-intensity intervals.
- **Duration:** 25–40 minutes per session.
- **Intensity:** 50–70% max heart rate (mostly conversational; some sessions slightly harder).
- **Timing:** On non-lifting days or 30+ minutes after lifting (not before).
- **Total Weekly Volume:** 60–120 minutes.

**Rationale:** Phase 2 has 4 lifting days/week, so cardio is strategically placed on non-lifting days or after lifting to avoid interfering with strength training performance. Moderate volume supports fat loss (300–500 kcal/week) without excessive fatigue.

**Option B: Moderate-Intensity Intervals (Optional, 1x/week)**

**Rationale:** One moderate-intensity session per week can boost fat loss and cardiovascular fitness without excessive fatigue. Keep intervals short and recovery periods adequate.

**Protocol: 20–30 Minute Session**

**Warm-up (5 minutes):**
- Easy pace (RPE 4/10).

**Main Set (15–20 minutes):**
- **Interval 1:** 2 minutes at RPE 6–7/10 (moderate effort; slightly elevated heart rate).
- **Recovery:** 2 minutes at RPE 4–5/10 (easy).
- **Repeat:** 4–5 times.

**Cool-down (5 minutes):**
- Easy pace (RPE 4/10).

**Total Energy Expenditure:** ~200–250 kcal.

**Examples:**

**Treadmill Intervals:**
- Warm-up: 3.5 mph, 0% incline, 5 min.
- Interval: 4.5 mph, 2% incline, 2 min (RPE 6–7).
- Recovery: 3.5 mph, 0% incline, 2 min (RPE 4–5).
- Repeat 4–5 times.
- Cool-down: 3.5 mph, 0% incline, 5 min.

**Cycling Intervals:**
- Warm-up: Easy pace, low resistance, 5 min.
- Interval: Moderate resistance, 2 min (RPE 6–7).
- Recovery: Low resistance, 2 min (RPE 4–5).
- Repeat 4–5 times.
- Cool-down: Easy pace, low resistance, 5 min.

**Rowing Intervals:**
- Warm-up: Easy strokes, 5 min.
- Interval: Faster strokes, moderate resistance, 2 min (RPE 6–7).
- Recovery: Slower strokes, low resistance, 2 min (RPE 4–5).
- Repeat 4–5 times.
- Cool-down: Easy strokes, 5 min.

## RATIONALE FOR INTENSIFICATION

Your client is experiencing the "honeymoon phase" of training—high motivation, good recovery, and positive momentum. This is an **optimal window to push training intensity** and capitalise on neural adaptations and hypertrophy stimulus.

**However, with PCOS, we must intensify *strategically*:**
- ✅ **Increase training stimulus** (heavier loads, more volume, higher RPE).
- ✅ **Maintain adequate nutrition** (no under-fuelling despite increased intensity).
- ✅ **Monitor recovery closely** (sleep, menstrual cycle, subjective wellbeing).
- ⚠️ **Avoid excessive volume** (more is not always better for PCOS; quality > quantity).

**Expected Outcomes:**
- Faster strength gains (5–10% increase in main lifts over 4 weeks).
- Greater hypertrophy stimulus (muscle building).
- Improved metabolic health (higher insulin sensitivity).
- Maintained or improved cycle regularity (with adequate nutrition).

### PHASE 1 NUTRITION GUIDELINES

**Hydration:**
- Aim for 2.5–3 litres of water daily (more on training days).
- Monitor urine colour (pale yellow = well-hydrated).
- Avoid excessive caffeine (>200 mg/day), which can worsen insulin resistance.

**Fibre:**
- Target 25–30g/day from whole grains, vegetables, legumes, and fruits.
- Fibre slows carbohydrate digestion, stabilising blood glucose.
- Increase gradually to avoid GI distress.

**Micronutrient Supplementation:**
- **Inositol (myo-inositol + D-chiro-inositol, 40:1 ratio):** 2–4g/day. Evidence-based for PCOS; improves insulin sensitivity and cycle regularity.
- **Vitamin D:** 1,000–2,000 IU/day (or test levels; many PCOS patients are deficient).
- **Omega-3 (fish oil or algae):** 1–2g EPA+DHA/day. Anti-inflammatory; supports hormonal health.
- **Magnesium:** 300–400mg/day. Supports insulin sensitivity and cycle regularity.
- **Chromium:** 200 mcg/day (optional). May improve glucose metabolism.

**Alcohol:**
- Limit to 0–1 drink per day (if any). Alcohol impairs glucose control and increases inflammation.

**Processed Foods & Added Sugars:**
- Minimise refined carbs, sugary drinks, and processed foods.
- Read labels; aim for <5g added sugar per serving.
- Focus on whole, nutrient-dense foods.

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This 12-week programme prioritises **metabolic health and insulin sensitivity** through structured resistance training, strategic cardio, and carefully calibrated nutrition. - ✅ Resistance training as first-line therapy (endocrinologist recommendation).

- ✅ 1RM testing at Week 12 to celebrate strength gains.

**Micronutrient Supplementation:**
- **Inositol (myo-inositol + D-chiro-inositol, 40:1 ratio):** 2–4g/day. Evidence-based for PCOS; improves insulin sensitivity and cycle regularity.

- **Chromium:** 200 mcg/day (optional). May improve glucose metabolism.

- Limit to 0–1 drink per day (if any). Alcohol impairs glucose control and increases inflammation.

- Minimise refined carbs, sugary drinks, and processed foods.
- Read labels; aim for <5g added sugar per serving.
